Class OmieContractProvider

Namespace
NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services
Assembly
NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.dll

Omie Service Contracts, read whole (ListarContratos, paginated) and indexed by the contract number (cNumCtr) — the number a caller's own configuration stores, because it is what the user reads in Omie. A contract is a price registry: it carries the negotiated value and the validity period of one client, and is never billed through.

Listed whole and cached for NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieContractProvider.CacheDuration, never consulted one by one. A screen that shows contracts in a grid would otherwise ask Omie once per row, and Omie answers a burst of repeated calls with "Consumo redundante detectado" — which blocks the app_key for every other integration, not just the grid.

GetAsync(string, bool, CancellationToken)

One contract by the number (or internal code) the caller stored. Reads the same cached listing — asking for several contracts in a row costs Omie a single call, which is the whole point of listing instead of consulting.

GetByNumberAsync(bool, CancellationToken)

Contracts indexed by cNumCtr. With forceRefresh the cache is ignored and rewritten with whatever Omie returns — the explicit "reload from ERP" of a screen, not the screen's own load.

NormalizeNumber(string?)

The key both sides of the match are reduced to: letters and digits only, upper-cased. Everything else — spaces, dots, slashes, hyphens — is dropped.

The contract number is read off a screen and typed into the caller's configuration by hand, so "CTR 001/2026", "ctr-001-2026" and "CTR0012026" are the same contract for the person typing it, and matching them literally would report a contract that plainly exists in Omie as missing. Callers must run their stored number through this same function — GetAsync(string, bool, CancellationToken) does it for them.
